title: LinkedIn AI assistant for post reviews, not inbox outreach
h1: a linkedin assistant for posts worth reading
description: See what a Metal bot can do in LinkedIn: draft and publish posts, read page stats and company details. No inbox messages or connection requests.
answer: **turn a useful customer question into your next linkedin post.** a Metal bot can draft in chat, publish posts and read named posts, company details and selected statistics. as of 12 november 2026, the toolkit has 29 actions. it has no inbox messaging, connection requests or general people search. give it the source posts and choose the ai you already sign in to.
og_line: a content assistant with clear boundaries.

app.name: LinkedIn
app.intro: **give it the post that deserves a follow-up.** it can read that post, look up a profile or company, and gather available statistics. bring the links you want reviewed; the connection has no general people search.

highlight.use: show which account your post would appear under
pull the company description before drafting a post about it
read the post you linked before writing a follow-up
bring the share statistics into your monday review
pull your organisation page statistics for the team meeting
show who reacted to the post you named
add the comment you read and approved

app.setup: **start by asking which account is connected.** connect linkedin, confirm the identity and give the bot reading access. add the post links or company you want reviewed. private company stats still depend on what your linkedin account can see.

routines_intro: **get the page review before the meeting and the draft before you need to post.** these jobs work from named posts and companies, with proposed copy kept in dusk. they need no feed reader or inbox watcher.

routines.name: page review before the team meeting
routines.message: every monday at 11, read available linkedin page statistics for the organisation named in your memory notes. show each returned measure with its reporting period. flag missing data. don't claim a campaign caused a change without evidence. return the note here. never change or publish anything.
routines.output: a page review with reporting periods and visible gaps

routines.name: follow-up from a post you pick
routines.message: every wednesday at 2, read the linkedin post links added this week to the content review file in our project folder. pick one with a useful unanswered question. show its source, the question and proposed follow-up wording here. if there are no new links, say so briefly. never publish or comment.
routines.output: one follow-up proposal tied to a named source post

routines.name: company wording check
routines.message: on the first day each month at 10, read linkedin company information for the company named in your memory notes. compare its returned description with the approved company description file in our project folder. list wording differences here. never edit the company page or claim you can.
routines.output: a comparison with the approved company description

asks:
**read the public words while they're still a private draft.** posts and comments ask first by default. a daily amount lets them go out within that limit.

careful with **Full access**: a bot there with no sending rule can send up to 25 a day without asking. give it **Ask every time**.

read only blocks uploads, publication and deletion. if you enable changes, allow the exact actions needed. for changes beyond sending, add 'ask me before changing anything'.
cannot: **no inbox outreach.** none of the 29 actions reads or sends linkedin direct messages.
**no connection requests or general people search.** ad targeting search doesn't replace either one.
**no full feed or comment-inbox digest.** you can read named posts and reactions, and create comments. there's no general feed reader or comment list.
**no linkedin event triggers.** use scheduled reads rather than promising instant alerts.
**no local review while your computer sleeps.** dusk cloud keeps schedules running with your desktop off.

sections.h: give the writer facts it can point to
sections.md:
**give the writer a fact worth saying in public.** keep approved wording and source post links in a file. tell the bot which facts it may use.

for [social posting](/use-cases/social-media-posting), decide who reviews before enabling publication. for [lead research](/use-cases/lead-research), use a separate workflow. this connection can't find people, email addresses or phone numbers.

**put the measure and reporting period where the team can see them.** choose measures your team already uses. a reaction increase says people reacted; sales need their own evidence.

have the report name unavailable statistics so the team knows which questions remain open.

faq.q: can a linkedin ai agent send connection requests and messages?
faq.a: **not through this toolkit.** neither appears among its 29 actions. it supports posts and comments, with sending approval by default.

faq.q: can claude write my linkedin posts?
faq.a: **yes. ask a Metal bot to draft in chat.** choose the ai and provide approved facts and source posts. publishing uses a separate action if you allow it later.

faq.q: can it monitor every new comment automatically?
faq.a: **no. there are no event triggers or comment-listing action.** ask for a scheduled review of specific posts instead.

review.by: lead agent: independent reviewer pass against seo/facts (4 reviewers), every finding applied, automated gate

steps: ask the bot to confirm the account
give it one post to review
ask for a follow-up draft in dusk chat only

mistakes.fix: the toolkit has no inbox messaging or connection requests.

mistakes.mistake: calling a reaction increase a sales result
mistakes.fix: report the measure and period. keep causal guesses out.

items: every company claim has a source
the wording has a human reviewer
sending is set to ask every time

tip.text: one post worth answering beats a calendar full of copy with nothing to say.
